scenario:
[LREG.5.2] The `s` flag makes `.` match a newline. `/a.b/s` against "a\nb" matches; without `s` it does not, because `.` excludes `\n` by default. Answer differs by flag alone, which is the only way to observe `s` under boolean matching.

POSIX ERE has no dotall: an engine that drops `s` reads `/a.b/s` and `/a.b/` as one pattern.

Unlike `m` (see LREG.5.2_re2_multiline_flag, where the obvious RE2 Option is dead code) `s` really is a plain Option: re2.h lists dot_nl outside the posix_syntax-only group, so ds_re2_compile sets it directly. This vector is what makes that a measurement rather than a reading of the header.

PATH PINNED: `FN_REGEX_MATCH`'s flags argument through `ds_re2_compile` (libds) and `ds.re2` (Mercury). `msg` is `String?` so the match stays a beta join test: a decided match on a non-nullable slot is an alpha REGEX test with the flag folded into its pattern (RLOW.5.2.2), which never reaches the flags argument and has its own vector, `RLOW.5.2.2_alpha_regex_flags`.

Expected count 2 = the Log fact plus the emitted Hit.
rules_ds:
schema Log scope logical:
    id: Int key
    msg: String? mutable

schema Hit scope logical:
    d: Int key

rule r:
    Log e where e.msg ~ /a.b/s
->
    emit Hit logical d: 0
